subject.title: [Feature]: Define a safe scale-to-zero recovery contract for Gateway hosts

question: Should OpenClaw standardize the proposed recovery-point and restored-admission contract in core, or should hosts compose the existing suspension, snapshot, and cron-projection seams without a new generic core lifecycle API?
rationale: The answer sets a durable core-versus-host ownership boundary across state, scheduling, admission, and compute lifecycle; source review cannot safely choose that product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Define only the owner inventory, verified recovery-point, and restored-admission identities in core, while hosts retain ingress, payloads, wake, placement, and destruction policy.

options.title: Keep composition host-owned
options.body: Document and support composition of the existing suspension, snapshot, and cron hooks without adding a new generic recovery lifecycle API.

options.title: Defer pending the linked slices
options.body: Wait for the open implementation slices to demonstrate the smallest missing invariant before choosing a permanent public contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define only the owner inventory, verified recovery-point, and restored-admission identities in core, while hosts retain ingress, payloads, wake, placement, and destruction policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Gateway suspension and cron hook history makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the core boundary decision.
